ai.title: Opus 4.6 replaces 4.5 in agent model definitions
ai.summary: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6 replaces Opus 4.5 across CLI agent wrappers and editor orchestrators. Updates apply to claude-code-cli.ts, codex-cli.ts, gemini-cli.ts, and base2.ts, plus best-of-n selectors and implementors in agents-graveyard. Prompt formatting for <think> tags adjusted to match new model behavior.

eli5.text: The software that runs automated coding tasks has switched its main helper to a newer version of an AI model called Opus 4.6. If you use tools that let AI write or review code for you, they are now using this newer helper starting today. The change quietly swapped out the old model for the new one in several places where these AI coding assistants are configured, which you would see if you checked the settings.

ai.title: CLI version bump to 1.0.613
ai.summary: The cli/release/package.json manifest bumped the codebuff CLI version from 1.0.612 to 1.0.613, packaging all user-visible changes already landed since the previous release. This release ships Bearer-token auth on the preferences API (fixing CLI updates to fallbackToALaCarte in production), strips the Pure Usage subscription and its stripe_price_id column via migration 0041_nappy_nebula.sql, and adds 'anthropic/claude-opus-4.6' to the OpenRouter-to-Anthropic model mapping. It also rolls Opus 4.5 out of CLI agent wrappers and editor orchestrators (claude-code-cli.ts, codex-cli.ts, gemini-cli.ts, base2.ts) in favor of Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6, adjusting etc. tag prompt formatting for the new model behavior.
ai.evidence: Modified file cli/release/package.json; the version field changed from 1.0.612 to 1.0.613. Analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit with no other code changes in the diff.

eli5.text: This release upgrades the command-line assistant to version 1.0.613, bringing you the latest AI model updates and smoother account handling. The newest model supported is Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6, which replaces the older 4.5 version across the assistant, code editor integrations, and Gemini/CLI wrappers, meaning you get access to the most recent thinking and coding capabilities when you run the latest updates. Account preferences are now easier to manage without logging into a web browser first, because the app now accepts a simple token-based login on its preferences endpoint. The pricing page has clearer information about how you can subscribe for higher usage limits or pay per credit at 1 cent each. Older subscription options tied to per-token billing have also been removed.

ai.title: Add skill loading instruction to implementation step prompt
ai.summary: Adds a mandatory instruction to use the skill tool for loading relevant skills in the implementation step prompt. This change ensures the agent explicitly checks for and loads skills before proceeding with code implementation. The modification is contained within agents/base2/base2.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant begins writing code, it now always reminds itself to first load any relevant pre-built skills before doing the actual implementation work. This affects everyone who uses the coding agent, and if you watched closely you'd see an extra instruction step appear right at the start of every implementation attempt, making sure nothing useful gets overlooked. The change is live today.

ai.title: Docs soften speed claims
ai.summary: Replaced general 3x speedup claim with specific eval data in web/src/content/tips/what-makes-codebuff-unique.mdx. Changed headline to '100+ Seconds Faster Than Claude Code' and removed 'often completing tasks in 1/3 the time' in favor of 'often completing features in 1/3 the time'. Updated mechanism description to emphasize parallel agents, better file discovery, and reading related files in one go.

eli5.text: The marketing page that compares how fast two assistants are now shows a concrete number instead of a loose "three times faster" claim: it says Codebuff finishes a real feature roughly 100 seconds quicker than Claude Code on average. If you read the page, you'll see the headline now reads '100+ Seconds Faster Than Claude Code' and the explanation points to specific tricks like running multiple helpers in parallel and grabbing related files all at once instead of one by one. Nothing about how the assistants actually work changed today, the wording update just makes the public claim match the measured test results, so the comparison reads like stopwatch data rather than a rough boast.

ai.title: Free mode requests bypass credit depletion checks
ai.summary: Chat completions API now allows requests with cost_mode FREE to proceed even when user credit balance is zero or subscription quotas are exhausted. The _post.ts handler imports isFreeMode from @codebuff/common/constants/free-agents to identify these requests and skips the totalRemaining <= 0 and fallbackToALaCarte enforcement blocks. This ensures free agent/model combinations remain accessible to users without active credits. Scope limited to web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts and corresponding tests.

eli5.text: You can now use the assistant through the API even when you have no credits left, as long as you explicitly ask for a free request. When someone sends a request marked as 'free' in the system, the billing check gets skipped, so it won't be blocked for lack of credit balance. This only applies to specific agent and model combinations designated as free; regular requests still require available credits.
